state.lastRunNotes: Third consecutive down session driven by macro, not stock-specific catalysts: rising global bond yields (US 10Y ~4.79%, RBA ~70-80% priced for a Sept 29 hike, RBNZ already hiked) are compressing multiples hardest on long-duration growth names like XRO (-32%) and WTC (-27%), with no company-specific bad news behind either move. Volume across the whole watchlist remains well below average (vol_x 0.2-0.5), so there's no capitulation/panic signal to act on. Held PME is still well above its A$150 stop and carries a Buy consensus with an above-market price target; CBA and TLS show no adverse news. Holding all positions and cash (61% of NAV) unchanged; growth/core split (~37%/63% ex-cash) stays inside the 35-65% band.
